proposed_postulate_insertion_after_volum: For each current boundary $S=\partial\chi_t(V)$, surface integration is the finite-chart Riemann convention: for any continuous scalar $f$ on $S$, choose regular $C^1$ graph charts $X_j:U_j\subset\mathbb R^2\to S\cap O_j$ and a finite nonnegative subordinate smooth ambient partition $\chi_j$ with compact support in the chart neighborhoods and sum one on $S$, and put $\int_S f\,dS=\sum_j\int_{U_j}(\chi_j f)(X_j(y))\sqrt{\det(DX_j(y)^TDX_j(y))}\,dy$. Each parameter integrand is extended by zero outside $U_j$. These integrals are finite and independent of charts and partition; in graph coordinates the density is $\sqrt{1+|Dh|^2}$. The unit normal is the continuous outward normal, and vector surface integrals are componentwise. Thus all traction, work, heat and entropy fluxes below use the same boundary-area convention.
